cases.eval_name: Non-standard d12 roll on Windows PowerShell
cases.output:
I couldn't roll the d12, so there's no damage number yet. I didn't want to make one up. Three attempts failed: the skill's standard command was rejected by the shell, and two other random-number commands needed permission that wasn't granted in this session.

You can roll it yourself in PowerShell:

```powershell
Get-Random -Minimum 1 -Maximum 13
```

The maximum is 13 because `-Maximum` is exclusive, so this gives a number from 1 to 12. Add your Strength modifier and any Rage bonus to get the greataxe damage.

If you'd rather I roll, approve the command when it asks for permission and I'll try again.

assertions.text: Response includes the PowerShell Get-Random cmdlet
assertions.reasoning: The response includes a PowerShell code block that uses the Get-Random cmdlet: `Get-Random -Minimum 1 -Maximum 13`.

assertions.text: The Get-Random command sets -Maximum to 13 (or equivalently 12 + 1), accounting for the exclusive upper bound
assertions.reasoning: The output uses `Get-Random -Minimum 1 -Maximum 13` and says the maximum is 13 because -Maximum is exclusive, so the command returns 1 to 12. That meets the assertion.
The output gives the command `Get-Random -Minimum 1 -Maximum 13`, so -Minimum is set to 1.

assertions.text: The reported roll result is a single integer between 1 and 12 inclusive
assertions.reasoning: The output says the d12 roll failed and gives no result. It contains no number from 1 to 12 that it presents as a roll, so it doesn't meet the assertion.
